2026_05_TB_DAL.headline: Williams' interior pressure tests Daniels while Prescott reads Bowles' disguises
2026_05_TB_DAL.paragraph1: Ahead of Thursday's game in Dallas, Tampa Bay needed rookie Jalon Daniels to handle pressure better after protection breakdowns stalled his late drive against Green Bay. Cowboys defensive tackle Quinnen Williams had begun creating disruption inside, encouraging quick releases and movement throws as the Buccaneers' counter to prolonged dropbacks. Dallas faced a different chess match: Dak Prescott could attack downfield if Tampa Bay committed extra defenders to the rush, while Todd Bowles could disguise pressure to make Prescott hold the ball. Communication in protection on both sides shaped the available passing windows.
2026_05_TB_DAL.model_rationale: Williams' interior rush threatened Daniels' protection, but moving the pocket could neutralize pressure. Tampa Bay's disguised blitz looks challenged Prescott to identify coverage before committing downfield.
